result.rationale: The diff's server schema is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness refinement, while the client-side AddGuestsDialog adds `.refine((emails) => uniqueEmails.size === emails.length)`. The handler's `uniqueGuests` filter only compares `guest !== attendee.email` against existing booking attendees and the blacklist — never within the submitted batch — so duplicate guests within one request pass validation and `createMany` inserts duplicate Attendee rows. Mechanism fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: The server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness refinement that the client-side copy in AddGuestsDialog.tsx (lines 26-29) enforces, and the handler's filter (lines 74-78) only dedups against existing attendees, never within the submitted batch. A direct API call with guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"] passes validation and createMany inserts two Attendee rows for the same person on the same booking; the invariant exists only in one client's UI and any other caller (API consumer, future client, the two already-drifted copies) silently corrupts the attendee list.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: server-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/.../addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness like the client-side `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` (refine with `Set`). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed via `guests.filter(...)` only excluding emails already present in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not dedupe duplicates within the submitted `guests` array. Therefore an API call with `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` can pass validation and result in `createMany` inserting duplicate attendee rows for the same booking (no uniqueness constraint shown in this diff).
